title: Cross-model streaming and tool-call semantics validation for pinned model variants
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: Validate that every newly onboarded model (and pinned model variants) preserves streaming semantics and deterministic tool/function-calling behavior when published with a performance profile. Scope: run a cross-model test matrix that exercises streaming partial outputs, mid-stream function/tool call frames, cancellation/retry, and the interaction with quantized/optimized kernels implied by published perf profiles. Deliverables: 1) Test harness integrated into CI that can run per-model streaming + tool-call scenarios; 2) A compatibility matrix (Confluence) with pass/fail and mitigation notes; 3) A canary rollout plan and a regression alert tied to the existing eval suite; 4) PRs that gate model onboarding until passing results are present. Acceptance criteria: - For each model variant in the onboarding batch, streaming must preserve exact token ordering for prefix+stream sequences in at least 99/100 synthetic sessions. - Function/tool-call frames must be emitted as a single, well-formed event (not split across streaming chunks) or, if streamed incrementally, must include clear boundary metadata per our streaming protocol. - No silent truncation of function arguments when kernel quantization or KV cache path changes are applied by the perf profile. - Latency regression vs benchmark profile must be within the defined threshold (<20% of profile SLO) for pinned variants in staging. - Canary traffic must show no more than 0.5% error-rate increase and no high-severity customer-impacting differences in outputs as measured by eval suites. - Concurrency/batching stress test (1000 concurrent sessions in staging dedicated pool) should not cause re-ordered function-call events. Out of scope: model architecture-level fixes (those are part of model ingestion work), long-tail corner cases unrelated to streaming/tool-call (to be captured in follow-ups).
comments: 2025-02-18 - Triage: created after PM asks for stronger guarantees around pinned model behavior when publishing perf profiles. Assigned to Mateo. Referenced ENG-21456 for prior streaming edge investigations.

2025-02-20 - Design review with Priya (PM) and Liam (SDK): agreed to require both structured boundary metadata and an end-to-end golden transcript for each model variant. Decision: if a model's runtime emits tool-call JSON across multiple chunks without metadata, fail onboarding.

2025-02-24 - Engineering note: implemented streaming-test harness in runtime-tests repo. Initial run identified 3 models where function args were split across chunk boundaries when using 4-bit quant kernels. Raised runtime PR #3821 to add chunk-boundary markers.

2025-02-25 - QA: added golden transcripts for 12 models and a differential checker that compares tool-call token sequences between baseline and candidate. Found one case of argument truncation after prefix caching was enabled. Created follow-up ENG-22778 for KV cache truncation fix.

2025-02-27 - PR feedback: runtime PR #3821 needs unit tests for streaming boundary metadata and an integration test that simulates partial tool-call emission under batching. Mateo added tests and requested review from Rahul.

2025-03-01 - Canary plan drafted: run canary across staging-dedicated-1 for 48 hours with 5% production-weighted traffic from synthetic harness. Monitor token-level diffs, function-call success ratios, and per-route latency. If >0.5% error increase, automatic rollback to previous model variant is triggered. Plan uploaded to Confluence.
Next steps: complete PR reviews, merge runtime fixes, run full onboarding matrix (estimated 24h for the batch), and file gating record in model-catalog when all passes are green.
